recipes.name: Old-World Cabbage Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can peeled and diced tomatoes

steps.text: Place chopped cabbage into an 8-quart soup pot.
Microwave diced carrot in 2 tablespoons water for 6 minutes on high.
Microwave diced celery in 2 tablespoons water for 4 minutes on high.

Add the microwaved vegetables to the pot. Add minced sweet onion, celery, and ketchup. Add juice cocktail, vegetable broth, chicken broth, and tomatoes. Fill each can with water, and add the water to the mixture. Cover, and bring to a boil. Continue boiling for 30 minutes.
Reduce heat to simmer and cook for 2 to 3 hours.
Serve with slices of a French baguette. Have salt, black pepper, and Tabasco available to season to taste at the table.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-World Cabbage Soup
raw_recipe.description: Cabbage, carrots, celery, sweet onion, and just the right amount of ketchup (yes, ketchup) make this lovely vegetable soup. Best if cooked one day ahead, refrigerated overnight and heated just before serving.

review.reviewBody: Delicious soup! I added a can of drained cannellini (white kidney) beans during the last 15 minutes of simmering. (A restaurant we visited served a White Bean and Cabbage Soup so I went searching for a recipe and came upon this one.) An 11.5 oz can of V-8 is just the right size to use in this recipe since it equates roughly to 1 1/2 cups. I chopped the cabbage very finely, and I added 2 cloves of fresh garlic minced, 1 tsp. salt, 1/2 tsp. black pepper, and 1/4 tsp. Tabasco when I added the broths. Save yourself time and effort - there is absolutely no need to microwave the carrots and celery - just add them in raw along with the other ingredients. I only added 2 cans of water since I prefer a thick soup, and I brought the soup to a boil and then lowered the temp. to simmer it for 2 hours. Didn't see the need to boil the soup for 30 minutes in addition to 2 hrs. of simmering! The soup turned out perfectly, and the black pepper along with the Tabasco gave it a very slight bite. This is a keeper!

This is good. I put mine in my crockpot and let it simmer for about six hours. I also added a pound of ground turkey to make it a meal. Next time, I will use more turkey. Everyone, even my 12 year-old, liked it.
Really good soup. I found that if I sub tomato paste for the ketchup, it helps get rid of the sweetness. Also, I do t precook any of the veggies in the microwave before hand.

Had to make a few substitutions, all the processed items mainly, except for the vegetable-tomato used V-8. All other items are made fresh and avoided microwaving items, insta-pot cooked instead. Processed food seems to take out the rich flavors of fresh produce. The soup came out marvelous!

It was a very tasty soup, however, I also found it quite sweet. My husband added a capful of vinegar and that neutralized it. We also added rice to it. Next time, I will use garden cocktail or clamato, not V8.

"An idealist is one who, on noticing that a rose smells better than a cabbage, concludes that it will also make better soup." -- H.L. Mencken Made it the first time as written. Excellent. The second time I added hot Italian sausage - also excellent. Next time I may add sliced mushrooms and chopped up fennel. Some 1" cuts of string beans might be nice too.... All those added tweaks are just fun for me. The original recipe is nonpareil without them. (Oh, and I double the amount and freeze individual bowl-sized portions.) I'm curious about microwaving the carrots and the celery. What's that all about? Edit: I did follow up with mushrooms, fennel, etc. All they did was gunk up a really good, but simple recipe. Back to the original with a small handful of caraway seeds.

Made this last yesterday. Assembled all ingredients--not following exactly. I substituted pre sliced coleslaw, purple, red, carrot slivers and used more than half the package. Used pre sliced fresh carrots and four stalks of celery plus onion. I reduced the ketchup to a little less than 1/2 a cup. Added the rest of the cans, but finished up by putting vegetable soup in one of the cans to be filled with water. Stirred it and set to boil. After simmering one hour, I tasted and added some pepper. Stirred occasionally, and decided it was done at not quite two hours. Tasted and shocked! The soup was outrageously good. Easy, satisfying and healthy.

I love trying different recipes for cabbage soup and this is by far the best yet. To make it easier for me, I put all ingredients in a slow cooker and it came out so good. Totally healthy and filling. Next time I think I will add some potatoes.
Tremendous flavor. Cook as is. But, I cooked for three hours on low (simmer) and this was an improvement. No extra spices are needed. ENJOY

I used whatever I had in the house...I had no cabbage, so I used a package of frozen brussels sprouts. I threw in a bag of frozen mixed vegetables, along with the carrots and celery. I deleted the chicken soup and used vegetable broth and a can of petite diced tomatoes with their liquid. So good. While I was rummaging around in the freezer, I found a half pound of leftover frozen shrimp, so I threw them in at the end, as well. It was so delicious. Even better the next day, as leftovers!

Just like my Polish Mom’s cabbage soup except added red wine vinegar and lemon juice too add the tangy zing that was missing. Also, no ketchup as I thought it would be too sweet. Used stewed tomatoes, beef & chicken stock, a little vegetable cocktail and water. Came out great!!!
enjoyed it... will bump up the flavor more next time

This mimics my granny's hamburger cabbage soup which is one of my absolute favorites to make . I omit the celery but I add corn...canned corn. Trust me, the canned corn brings flavor that you just can't get from fresh or frozen.Also I just beef bone broth instead of chicken broth ...and NO ketchup.Put it in the crock pot and let her just simmer all day....the smell is intoxicating, the flavor is even better.
Tasty, healthy soup, especially tasty if you let it sit in the fridge for a day. Tasty, healthy and only 39 calories a serving, cannot beat that!
I followed this recipe to the T. This definitely is not old world cabbage soup. It has a decent flavor but it’s not what I was expecting
Not the way we made it to many different juiy

Outstanding soup. I wanted to make it vegan so I switched out the chicken stock for the vegetable broth. Then I found a vegan Protein Vegetable broth I found at Walmart. And I used a 28 oz can off the diced tomatoes. To spice it up some I added about two teaspoons of Tony Chachere’s. The result was great.

I made this recipe as is and it was very good. However, I do not understand how you can call this "Old World Cabbage Soup" as the "Old World" did not have tomato-vegetable juice cocktail or canned chicken broth. That's just taking too much liberty with the title of this recipe.
